answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to lock a stake bond in a shared registry before it can transact. Attestations are weighted by stake and by a reputation kernel that decays unless the agent keeps doing verifiable work, so one operator cannot forge many influential identities from a single bond: splitting stake dilutes each copy. The sable line is economic: each fake identity must pay its own bond, and proven fraud triggers slashing that burns the stake, so large-scale fakery costs more than it can ever gain.
